subject: Erasure vs Redaction: PHI retention & options for MedConnect audit
messages:
From: Dr. Elena Ruiz <eruiz@medconnect.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Erasure vs Redaction: PHI retention & options for MedConnect audit

Hi Naomi,

We have an upcoming HIPAA readiness audit and MedConnect's security team is validating our vendors' data lifecycle capabilities. Two quick asks where we need clarity from Redwood before next Friday:

1) For PHI contained in text generation calls (notes, transcripts) — can Redwood fully erase request+response pairs on demand, including any cached KV state used for inference?
2) If full erasure is not feasible or will impact SLA, can you describe supported redaction/pseudonymization options (deterministic pseudonymization, token masking, redact-then-embed workflows) and their guarantees (irreversibility, auditability)?

We're trying to finalize our vendor questionnaire and mutual action plan (MAP). Any short doc or matrix mapping options -> tradeoffs (latency, recovery, audit evidence) would be helpful.

Thanks — can you loop in engineering and legal for scope and timeline?

Best,
Elena
Dr. Elena Ruiz
Head of Compliance, MedConnect Health

----
MedConnect is a clinical network; audit window: week of 5/17.
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Elena Ruiz <eruiz@medconnect.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, MedConnect Compliance <compliance@medconnect.com>

Subject: Re: Erasure vs Redaction: PHI retention & options for MedConnect audit

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the heads-up about the audit window. Looping in Marcus (serving runtime) and Monica (customer privacy/legal) to provide concrete options. High level summary in advance, and I attached a short matrix and a proposed erase-playbook (see attachments).

Summary (short):
- Full erasure: We can support customer-initiated permanent deletion of stored request/response logs and artifacts within our hosted offering. This covers persistent storage, logging layers, and model-store artifacts. Impact: deletes trace of the content but does not retroactively remove model parameters (we never train on customer requests in hosted products). KV caches used for active sessions are purged on deletion requests and can be scheduled immediate or at next idle window.

- Redaction/pseudonymization: We offer two patterns:
  1) Client-side redaction: Customer redacts PII/PHI before sending to Redwood (recommended when customer controls UI/data).
  2) Server-side structured redaction pipeline: token masking + deterministic pseudonymization (salted hash mapping stored in HSM-backed KMS if requested) or irreversible redaction (irreversible token removal).

Tradeoffs:
- Irreversible redaction (zero-knowledge removal) = best privacy guarantees but you lose the ability to re-link or rehydrate records; useful for long-term retention minima.
- Deterministic pseudonymization = allows re-link (if you hold mapping) and supports analytics; requires secure mapping storage and access controls.

Requested next steps:
1) Marcus & team to confirm KV-cache deletion timeline and what we can commit to for on-demand erase (immediate vs within 24 hours).
2) Monica to provide suggested contract language and evidence types (deletion confirmation, audit logs, certificate).
3) We'll propose a one-hour call tomorrow to walk the MAP and finalize the matrix.

Note: attachments: redaction_options_matrix.xlsx (matrix of options, SLO impact, audit artifacts) and proposed-map-erase-playbook.pdf (step-by-step procedure + owner).

--
Naomi Feldman
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Erasure vs Redaction: PHI retention & options for MedConnect audit

Thanks Naomi — quick engineering notes and constraints from the serving/runtime side:

- On-demand deletion: for hosted customers we can delete request/response logs, user-level metadata, and any derived artifacts (stored embeddings, reranker indices) on demand. Our deletion flow: tombstone -> async purge from primary stores -> background reclaim; typical completion: 1-24 hours depending on object size and whether data exists in backups.

- KV cache (in-memory + persisted warm caches):
  * In-memory session KV: purged immediately when session terminated or on deletion request.
  * Warm persisted KV caches (used for faster cold-starts across sessions) are stored encrypted; we can purge entries for a customer by ID within our cache tier. Purge typically completes within 15 minutes but depends on replication windows.

- Embeddings & indexes: If you persist embeddings into Redwood-managed indexes, deletion will remove vectors and rebuild shards; vector removal is eventual and may take up to 48 hours for full compaction. If you host embeddings externally (customer-managed), you control retention.

- Audit evidence: we can emit signed deletion events and a deletion certificate including object ids and timestamps. We record a UUID per erase request and keep a deletion audit log (immutable append-only) for 7 years by default (configurable for enterprise).

- Redaction: server-side token masking is straightforward (regex + NLP entity detection). Irreversible redaction means removing tokens before they persist anywhere; pseudonymization stores mapping in a KMS-protected store — we recommend HSM-backed KMS for re-identification use cases.

Open engineering question for SLAs: do you require synchronous confirmation (block until deletion done) vs asynchronous notification? Synchronous adds latency and operational complexity.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Erasure vs Redaction: PHI retention & options for MedConnect audit

Hi Elena — adding legal/compliance framing and suggested contractual language for the MAP. A few points to incorporate into the vendor questionnaire and into the contract addendum:

- Regulatory baseline: HIPAA requires covered entities to maintain required documentation; however vendor retention obligations are negotiable. For purposes of a minimum binding commitment we typically offer:
  * Data retention: customer-controlled; Redwood will purge customer request/response data on verified deletion requests. Redwood will not use customer content to improve models in hosted offerings.
  * Minimum retention period for audit logs/deletion certificates: 6 years (HIPAA baseline). We can extend to 7/10 years upon enterprise agreement.

- Deletion evidence: We can provide a signed deletion certificate, immutable deletion audit record (uuid + timestamp + object ids), and a snapshot of the purge runbook. These are acceptable artifacts in most audits. If MedConnect requires a certified third-party attestation, we can coordinate via our SOC2 report and an agreed audit scope.

- Redaction policy language (suggested clause): "Vendor will provide server-side irreversible redaction and deterministic pseudonymization options. Irreversible redaction will permanently remove specified data values such that re-identification is computationally infeasible. Deterministic pseudonymization will use customer-scoped salts managed in the customer's KMS when requested."

- Recommended MAP items:
  1) Finalize whether MedConnect wants irreversible deletion vs pseudonymization for retained records.
  2) Decide on deletion SLA (immediate/24h/48h) and whether synchronous confirmation is required.
  3) Confirm retention period for deletion audit evidence (we propose 6 years default).

If that's acceptable I'll draft a short addendum and send a one-pager for signatures.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Dr. Elena Ruiz <eruiz@medconnect.com>

Naomi/Monica/Marcus — this is perfect, thank you.

MedConnect preference: irreversible redaction for long-term archived records, deterministic pseudonymization for operational analytics with the mapping held by us (customer-managed KMS).

Audit asks: we will need a deletion certificate for any purge actions requested during the audit and the immutable deletion audit log for a 6-year window. Synchronous confirmation is not required — asynchronous deletion within 24 hours + signed certificate is acceptable.

Can you confirm timeline to deliver the addendum and the MAP so we can include them in our vendor binder? Also please attach the purge playbook PDF you mentioned (I see it referenced in Naomi's reply).

Thanks — will plan the audit call for Tue 5/18 10:00am PT unless you propose otherwise.

Best,
Elena
